name: option-type
what: An option type is a typed group of values, set on the registry, on a document or on a render request, that stages and lowering rules read.

entries.name: BlocksConfig
entries.summary: Which families of typographic substitution apply when the text of a document is resolved (curly quotes, dashes, ellipses). Fixed when the registry is built: it cannot vary per document or per render.

entries.name: HtmlRenderOptions
entries.summary: the page's title and language tag; whether the elements written for a node carry their position in the source; the stop written after a run-in heading's title; what the host delivers in place of the declared content of a stylesheet or script; the stylesheets and scripts the host requires for the page in addition to those its content requires; the tag each heading kind is written with; and the heading level written as `<h1>`. Set per render request.

entries.name: LatexRecomposedRenderOptions
entries.summary: how a non-ASCII character of the text is written (`declare`, the default, writes the character and declares it in the style file; `replace` writes its LaTeX spelling), and the spellings that replace the library's own for given characters; whether the document's source comments are left out; the LaTeX packages this library never requests, and the packages the style file always requests, with their options, merged with the requests that the document's content causes into one `\RequirePackage` line per package; three parts of LaTeX text written byte for byte into the style file, before the packages, after them and at its end; the user-definition names written as the document spells them rather than under a prefix, and those written as robust commands rather than expandable macros; the stem of the style file's name (default `flmrecomposed`), to which the program's naming of files may add a prefix; when the style file is written (`when-needed`, the default, writes it only where the document needs something in it, `always` writes it for every document, and either way it is written where packages to request always or LaTeX text to write into it are given); whether headings are written through the LaTeX hook `\flmHeading`, and labels and references through the LaTeX hooks `\flmLabels`, `\flmLabelsWithDisplayText` and `\flmRef` (both on by default); whether the labels of an equation line are left out of the recomposed LaTeX in a registry without the references feature (off by default; no effect where that feature is registered); and whether a proof's back-reference is written as the author wrote it, for the `phfthm` package (the default), or resolved into the LaTeX hook `\flmProofTitle`, for `amsthm` alone. Set per render request.

entries.name: LatexRenderedRenderOptions
entries.summary: the stem of the style file's name (default `flmx`), to which the program's naming of files may add a prefix; the stop written after a run-in heading's title; the LaTeX packages this backend never requests, for a template that loads them itself; the packages the style file always requests, with their options; and three parts of LaTeX text written byte for byte into the style file, after the engine check, after the packages and at its end. Set per render request.

entries.name: PiecesRenderOptions
entries.summary: the pieces placed although they are declared off by default (`include`), and the pieces declared on by default that are left out (`exclude`). Set per render request.

entries.name: TextRenderOptions
entries.summary: the line width in columns (null: never wrap), default 80; the width of a tab in columns, default 4; the stop written after a run-in heading's title, default `.`, the empty text for none; whether a link to an address outside the document prints the address after its content, default on; whether a link whose content already shows its address prints the address too, default off; and the heading level printed as a first-level heading, default 1. Set per render request.

entries.name: AnnotationsConfig
entries.summary: The annotators, in order, the first numbered 0: for each, the name of its command (without the backslash) and the initials shown at the start of its annotations. Fixed when the registry is built: it cannot vary per document or per render.

entries.name: AnnotationsRenderOptions
entries.summary: Whether every annotation is left out of the output, each highlight shown as its passage alone and each comment not at all (`hidden`, false by default). Set per render request.

entries.name: CellsConfig
entries.summary: Whether the `cells` environment can be written wherever blocks can (`global`, false by default), in addition to the bodies that refer to the scoped package `flm.cells.environment`, such as a `table` float's. Fixed when the registry is built: it cannot vary per document or per render.

entries.name: CitationsConfig
entries.summary: Where the citation entries are shown (`placement`: `listed` after the content, or `in-place` in the citation marks), how a citation mark shows its numbers (`mark`: `bracketed` or `superscript`), the citation counter style (`style`: the number format, the delimiters, the texts joining several numbers, whether consecutive numbers make a range, and the words `\R` writes), the heading above the list of cited works (`heading_title`, or null for no heading, and `heading_level`), and the text written between the numbers and a note (`note_separator`). Fixed when the registry is built: it cannot vary per document or per render.

entries.name: DeftermConfig
entries.summary: The lead-in of a term definition (the `defterm` environment): a template in which `#{term}` is the term being defined, or none for no lead-in. Fixed when the registry is built: it cannot vary per document or per render.

entries.name: FloatsConfig
entries.summary: The float types, each an environment of the type's name: its caption name, its numbering policy, its number format, the words a reference writes before its number, the content handlers it accepts, the scoped packages available in its body and the label types it accepts. Fixed when the registry is built: it cannot vary per document or per render.

entries.name: GraphicsConfig
entries.summary: Whether `\includegraphics` is also an ordinary command of the document (`global`, false by default), besides a command of the scoped package `flm.graphics.includegraphics`, which a float type can make available in its body (the `figure` and `table` types do). Fixed when the registry is built: it cannot vary per document or per render.

entries.name: GraphicsRenderOptions
entries.summary: How each output publishes its images (`strategy`: `reference`, `copy` or `data-uri`), the conversion rules it applies (`convert`), and the factors by which it multiplies the size of raster and of vector images (`magnification`: `raster` and `vector`, 1 by default), each a map from an output's name to its value. Set per render request.

entries.name: HeadingsConfig
entries.summary: The heading kinds and the heading commands that write them: each kind's level, counter, counter style, the counter it is numbered within, number format, heading title template, table-of-contents and run-in settings and reference point; each command's heading kind and default options; and which kinds are numbered. Fixed when the registry is built: it cannot vary per document or per render.

entries.name: HeadingsLatexOptions
entries.summary: The LaTeX sectioning command each heading kind is written as in the recomposed LaTeX, keyed by the kind's name; a kind not listed is written as the command of its own name. Set per render request.

entries.name: ListsConfig
entries.summary: The list environments: for each list kind, its environment name, whether its items are numbered, its label templates and its reference templates (read for a numbered list kind) by nesting depth, and its nesting joiner. Fixed when the registry is built: it cannot vary per document or per render.

entries.name: MathConfig
entries.summary: Whether the lines of `equation`, `align` and `gather` are numbered (`true` by default). Fixed when the registry is built: it cannot vary per document or per render.

entries.name: MathRecomposeOptions
entries.summary: How the recomposed LaTeX writes a display-math environment: the LaTeX written before and after it, and whether the environment is written through the command `\flmMathEnvironment`. Set per render request.

entries.name: DocMeta
entries.summary: the document's metadata: its title, its authors and its date, each an FLM text with the place it was written at, and every other key as data

entries.name: NumberingConfig
entries.summary: The counter styles that replace declared ones: each entry replaces, by its name, the counter style a feature declares. Fixed when the registry is built: it cannot vary per document or per render.

entries.name: NumberingOptions
entries.summary: Per counter, the counter it is numbered within and the value it has before it is first advanced. Set on the document; a render request may set it again, and its value then replaces the document's for that render.

entries.name: QuoteConfig
entries.summary: The quote environments, by name: for each, the quotation-section commands its body accepts (`text`, `lines`, `attributed`, `block`) and the kind of quotation section that content written outside those commands is read as (the key `bare`; when it is absent, such content is an error). Fixed when the registry is built: it cannot vary per document or per render.

entries.name: RefsRecomposeOptions
entries.summary: How the recomposed LaTeX writes labels and references: the label types written as the document wrote them instead of as generated keys, and whether a reference is protected against a command that changes the case of its argument. Set per render request.

entries.name: RefsConfig
entries.summary: The texts that join the items of a reference to several targets. Fixed when the registry is built: it cannot vary per document or per render.

entries.name: RefsRenderOptions
entries.summary: Whether a reference that points at no label is reported as an Error (the default) or, under `unresolved: allow`, as a Warning. Set per render request.

entries.name: TheoremsConfig
entries.summary: The theorem-like environments: the theorem classes (whether numbered, whether in the shared counter, the heading template, the closing mark, whether a proof's title is read as a back-reference), the theorem kinds (the class, the words, whether a proof is expected), the number format and the label types a numbered kind accepts. Fixed when the registry is built: it cannot vary per document or per render.

entries.name: TocOptions
entries.summary: The deepest heading level the table of contents lists (`depth`, 3 by default). Set on the document; a render request may set it again, and its value then replaces the document's for that render.

entries.name: UserdefsConfig
entries.summary: The user definitions (macros, environments and special character sequences defined by substitution), one map per kind, and the expansion depth limit. Fixed when the registry is built: it cannot vary per document or per render.

entries.name: XnotesConfig
entries.summary: The kinds of xnote (notes set apart from the running text, such as footnotes): for each kind, its commands, the words a reference writes, its label type, whether it is numbered, its number and mark templates, where its notes are shown, how its content is laid out, the title of its list, the text of the link back to the mark and the LaTeX command it is handed to. Fixed when the registry is built: it cannot vary per document or per render.

name: service-slot
what: A service slot is a named place where features and the embedding program contribute objects that stages use.

entries.name: flm.artifacts.namer
entries.summary: the host's naming scheme: the path of each artifact of an output, relative to the output location

entries.name: flm.cells.styles
entries.summary: the cell styles a cell's style tokens may refer to: the ones the `cells` feature ships and the ones other features contribute

entries.name: flm.citations.providers
entries.summary: The citation providers, which give the citation entries of the cited works and are asked in order for each cited key; the feature never requires one.

entries.name: flm.floats.content
entries.summary: The content handlers that float types list by name: each accepts a float's content or refuses it.

entries.name: flm.floats.types
entries.summary: The float types; `floats::contribute_type` declares each one, with the environment of its name.

entries.name: flm.graphics.converters
entries.summary: the converters that turn an image of one format into another, asked in the order contributed for each conversion rule an output applies

entries.name: flm.graphics.inspector
entries.summary: the inspector a host supplies, which reports what an image file states: whether it is a vector or a raster image, its size in pixels, its resolution and its physical size

entries.name: flm.graphics.resolver
entries.summary: the graphics resolver a host supplies, which finds the file for an image's path (its identity, its format, the address that reaches it) and reads its content when asked

entries.name: flm.latex.packages
entries.summary: the package definitions that a requirement identifier `flm.latex.pkg.<name>` resolves to

entries.name: flm.latex.preamble
entries.summary: the definition pieces a requirement identifier `flm.latex.def.<name>` resolves to

entries.name: flm.numbering.counters
entries.summary: The counters that reference points are numbered by, one value per counter: its name, the counter style its numbers are shown in, and the counter it is numbered within.

entries.name: flm.numbering.number-writers
entries.summary: The number writers registered by name, one value per number writer: code that turns the counter values to be shown in a counter style into the content a reader sees.

entries.name: flm.numbering.parent-sets
entries.summary: The parent sets, one value per set: a named list of counters within which a counter may be numbered; at each reference point, the counter of the set advanced most recently is the parent.

entries.name: flm.numbering.styles
entries.summary: The counter styles a number may be shown in, one value per counter style: the number format, the sub-levels, the word before the number, the delimiters and the texts that join several numbers.

entries.name: flm.numbering.within-joiners
entries.summary: The within-joiners registered by name, one value per within-joiner: code that writes, before a counter's number, the numbers of the counters it is numbered within.

entries.name: flm.output.regions
entries.summary: the outputs whose entry artifact is made of output regions, each with the table that holds its regions and the tables of the files written beside its entry artifact

entries.name: flm.pieces
entries.summary: the pieces each feature offers (document-level values a backend places before or after the content), in the order a backend places them

entries.name: flm.xnotes.kinds
entries.summary: the kinds of xnote, in order: the ones the `xnotes` feature's configuration declares and the ones other features contribute

name: scoped-package
what: A scoped package is a set of commands defined only inside certain environment bodies or arguments, such as the item command inside a list.

entries.name: flm.math.lines
entries.summary: The commands of a display-math environment's body: `\\`, `\label`, `\tag` and `\nonumber`.

entries.name: flm.refs.label
entries.summary: The command available in an argument that accepts labels: `\label{type:label}`.

entries.name: flm.lists.items
entries.summary: The command recognized inside a list environment's body: `\item`, which begins an item.

entries.name: flm.quote.sections.quote
entries.summary: The quotation-section commands available inside the body of the quote environment `quote`.

entries.name: flm.quote.lines
entries.summary: The commands available inside a lines section of a quotation: `\\`, which ends a line, and `\indent`, which indents the line it starts.

entries.name: flm.graphics.includegraphics
entries.summary: `\includegraphics[options]{path}`, in the bodies that refer to this package (those of a `figure` and a `table` by default).

entries.name: flm.floats.fields
entries.summary: The commands of a float's body, which the float reads: `\caption[alt=…]{…}`, `\label{…}` and `\nonumber`.

entries.name: flm.cells.environment
entries.summary: The `cells` environment, in the bodies that accept a table of cells.

entries.name: flm.cells.body
entries.summary: The instructions of a table of cells: `\cell`, `\celldata`, `\\`, `\rownames` and `\colnames`.

entries.name: flm.cells.merge
entries.summary: `\merge`, in the placement of a cell and the mapping of `\celldata`.

entries.name: flm.cells.data
entries.summary: `&`, in the data of `\celldata`.

name: presentation-element
what: A presentation element is an element of the trees a backend builds from the document's trees; it never appears in a parsed document.

entries.name: flm.pres.block
entries.summary: a block container with a role and kinds (a run of blocks)

entries.name: flm.pres.block-heading
entries.summary: a heading placed on its own between blocks, with its heading kind's name, a level and whether it is listed in a table of contents: a `body` content slot holding the title (inline content) and an optional `alt` content slot holding the alternative title

entries.name: flm.pres.cells
entries.summary: a table of cells: its grid in the payload, a `cell` content slot per entry

entries.name: flm.pres.deco-mark
entries.summary: the childless mark left where the lowering driver moved a decoration out of a content slot

entries.name: flm.pres.deco.final
entries.summary: a decoration closing its block (a proof's closing mark)

entries.name: flm.pres.deco.margin
entries.summary: a decoration set beside the text, level with its decoration mark

entries.name: flm.pres.deco.runin
entries.summary: a decoration at the start of its block (a theorem's heading)

entries.name: flm.pres.dropped
entries.summary: the childless mark where a rule left out something it could not place

entries.name: flm.pres.html.tag
entries.summary: one HTML tag: its name, its attributes, and either children or one piece of markup

entries.name: flm.pres.image
entries.summary: an image

entries.name: flm.pres.latex.definition
entries.summary: a macro or environment definition, or a feature's declaration, written to the style file and never where the node occurs

entries.name: flm.pres.latex.environment
entries.summary: a LaTeX environment: the content slots of its arguments, then the body

entries.name: flm.pres.latex.macro
entries.summary: a LaTeX macro call: the command name and one content slot per argument

entries.name: flm.pres.latex.raw
entries.summary: LaTeX text written byte for byte

entries.name: flm.pres.line
entries.summary: one line of a `lines` node, with its indentation and alignment

entries.name: flm.pres.lines
entries.summary: a sequence of lines

entries.name: flm.pres.link
entries.summary: a link around inline display content

entries.name: flm.pres.list
entries.summary: a list: a `label` and an `item` content slot per entry

entries.name: flm.pres.math-passthrough
entries.summary: mathematics passed through as source text: the formula's content as written, which the `math-passthrough` feature stages and nothing in FLM has read

entries.name: flm.pres.math-text
entries.summary: document content inside a formula: the argument of a text command

entries.name: flm.pres.par
entries.summary: a laid-out paragraph (an inline run)

entries.name: flm.pres.runin-heading
entries.summary: the title of a run-in heading, inside its run-in decoration, with the same payload and content slots as a block heading: a `body` slot holding the title (inline content) and an optional `alt` slot holding the alternative title

entries.name: flm.pres.span
entries.summary: inline content with a display style, a role and kinds

entries.name: flm.pres.subtree
entries.summary: the position at which another document tree is placed

entries.name: flm.pres.unknown
entries.summary: a macro or environment the parse could not attribute to any feature

entries.name: flm.pres.unsupported
entries.summary: the childless stand-in for a node the backend cannot render

entries.name: flm.pres.verbatim
entries.summary: byte-exact content of a verbatim kind (text, code or identifier), inline or as a block, with an optional language

name: piece
what: A piece is a value computed over the whole document, such as the list of footnotes, that a backend places before or after the document's content.

entries.name: flm.xnotes.list.footnote
entries.summary: the list of the `footnote` xnotes, after the document's content

entries.name: flm.citations.bibliography
entries.summary: the list of the cited works, placed after the document's content

entries.name: flm.meta.title
entries.summary: the document's title, before the content

entries.name: flm.meta.author
entries.summary: the document's authors, before the content

entries.name: flm.meta.date
entries.summary: the document's date, before the content

entries.name: flm.toc
entries.summary: the table of contents, before the content

name: style
what: A style definition is a part of a stylesheet that a backend writes into its output when a tree requires it.

entries.name: flm.headings.style
entries.summary: headings: no stylesheet of their own

entries.name: flm.xnotes.style
entries.summary: the line above a list of xnotes and the brackets around an xnote shown in place

entries.name: flm.defterm.style
entries.summary: the term being defined, where its own term definition uses it

entries.name: flm.theorems.style
entries.summary: the heading of a theorem: its name set apart from its title

entries.name: flm.quote.style
entries.summary: a quotation set apart from the text around it, and its attribution from its passage

entries.name: flm.floats.style
entries.summary: a float set apart from the text around it, with its content and the line under its content centered

entries.name: flm.cells.style
entries.summary: a table's outline and edge lines, a cell's padding and alignment, and the backgrounds of the custom styles `green`, `blue`, `yellow` and `red`

entries.name: flm.citations.style
entries.summary: the line height of a raised citation mark, which keeps the mark from pushing its line apart from the lines around it

entries.name: flm.meta.style
entries.summary: the document's title large and bold, and the authors and the date each on a line of its own, indented under the title

entries.name: flm.toc.style
entries.summary: the lists of the table of contents without a marker, each nested list indented, and a space after an entry's number

entries.name: flm.html.style.core
entries.summary: paragraphs, blocks, the display styles of a span, links, images and the three decorations

entries.name: flm.html.style.headings
entries.summary: the six heading sizes

entries.name: flm.html.style.verbatim
entries.summary: content set character for character, inline and as a block

entries.name: flm.html.style.math-passthrough
entries.summary: a displayed formula, and content written inside a formula

entries.name: flm.html.style.lists
entries.summary: lists with their entries and labels, and a run of lines with its alignment

entries.name: flm.html.style.errors
entries.summary: what the page shows where the document asked for something that could not be produced

entries.name: flm.html.style.page
entries.summary: the page's own typography and the width the content is held to; required by the page this backend assembles and by no element

name: script
what: A script definition is a part of a script that a backend writes into its output when a tree requires it.

entries.name: flm.html.mathjax
entries.summary: the formula renderer: its configuration, then the address its program is loaded from

name: settings-key
what: A settings key is one value of a feature's settings, written under the feature's name; this list gives each key as the feature's name, a dot and the key.

entries.name: blocks.auto_unicode_quotes
entries.summary:
Whether the straight double quote `"` and the straight single quote `'`
become curly quotes, opening (`“`, `‘`) or closing (`”`, `’`) according
to their position. When
`ligature_unicode_quotes` is
also on, the two-character ligature `''` is that family's, and this test
applies to a single `'`.

entries.name: blocks.ligature_unicode_quotes
entries.summary:
Whether the TeX quote ligatures apply: ``` `` ``` becomes `“`, `''`
becomes `”`, and `` ` `` becomes `‘`. A single `'` becomes `’`, as in
TeX, only when `auto_unicode_quotes` is
off; when both families are on, the position test of
`auto_unicode_quotes` decides a single `'`.

entries.name: blocks.ligature_unicode_dashes
entries.summary:
Whether the TeX dash ligatures apply: `---` becomes an em dash `—` and
`--` an en dash `–`.

entries.name: blocks.ligature_unicode_ellipses
entries.summary: Whether the ellipsis ligature applies: `...` becomes `…`.

entries.name: numbering.styles
entries.summary:
The replacements, each replacing the counter style declaration of the
same name, in the order they were given.

entries.name: numbering.counters
entries.summary: What the document says about each counter it mentions, in name order.

entries.name: math.numbered_equations
entries.summary:
Whether the lines of `equation`, `align` and `gather` that carry no
`\nonumber` and no `\tag` are numbered. `true` by default. The lines
of `equation*`, `align*` and `gather*` are never numbered.

entries.name: math.surround_display_math
entries.summary:
The LaTeX written, byte for byte, before and after every displayed
formula: every display-math environment and every displayed math group
(`\[…\]`). Both empty by default.

entries.name: math.emit_flm_math_environment_macro
entries.summary:
Whether an environment is written as
`\flmMathEnvironment{<name>}{<arguments>}{<body>}` rather than as
`\begin{<name>}…\end{<name>}`. Off by default. The style file then
holds the definition of `\flmMathEnvironment`, which a user may
redefine.

entries.name: refs.join
entries.summary:
The texts that join the items of a reference to several targets.
Default: the defaults of `JoinDecl`.

entries.name: refs.unresolved
entries.summary:
The severity of a reference that points at no label: `error` (the
default) or `allow` (a Warning).

entries.name: refs.safe_label_types
entries.summary:
Per label type (`sec`, `eq`), how its labels are written; a type not
listed is `Safe`. Empty by default. A label
with no type belongs to none of these and is always written by its
safe label.

entries.name: refs.protect
entries.summary:
Whether a reference is wrapped in `\NoCaseChange{\protect …}`, which
keeps it out of a command that changes the case of its argument
(`\MakeUppercase`). Off by default; when on, the style file requests
the `textcase` package, which supplies `\NoCaseChange` on every LaTeX
kernel.

entries.name: headings.headings
entries.summary: The heading kinds, in the order they were given.

entries.name: headings.commands
entries.summary: The heading commands, in the order they were given.

entries.name: headings.numbering
entries.summary:
Which kinds are numbered: `HeadingNumbering::NothingNumbered` by
default.

entries.name: headings.latex_commands
entries.summary:
The LaTeX sectioning command, without the backslash, that each heading
kind is written as, keyed by the kind's name. A kind the map does not list
is written as the command of its own name. Empty by default.

entries.name: lists.environments
entries.summary: The list kinds, by environment name.

entries.name: xnotes.kinds
entries.summary: The xnote kinds, in the order in which their lists are placed.

entries.name: defterm.lead_in
entries.summary:
The lead-in template, or `None` for no lead-in. `DEFAULT_LEAD_IN`
by default.

entries.name: theorems.classes
entries.summary: The theorem classes, by name.

entries.name: theorems.kinds
entries.summary: The theorem kinds, by environment name.

entries.name: theorems.number_format
entries.summary:
The number format every kind's number is written in, a number
template of the numbering feature, `#{arabic}` by default. To write
one kind's number otherwise, a host replaces that kind's counter style
(`flm.theorems.style.<kind>`, see `numbers`) by name
through the numbering feature's configuration.

entries.name: theorems.label_types
entries.summary:
The label types that every numbered kind accepts on a `\label` written
on one of its theorems; `DEFAULT_LABEL_TYPES` by default. A theorem
of an unnumbered kind accepts no label.

entries.name: quote.environments
entries.summary: The quote environments, by name.

entries.name: annotations.annotators
entries.summary:
The annotators, in order: the first is annotator 0. In settings, a map
from each annotator's command name to its other fields.

entries.name: annotations.hidden
entries.summary:
Whether every annotation is left out of the output, each highlight
shown as its passage alone and each comment not at all. `false` by
default.

entries.name: graphics.global
entries.summary:
Whether `\includegraphics` is also an ordinary command of the
document, which can be written wherever text can, besides a command of
its scoped package. `false` by default.

entries.name: graphics.strategy
entries.summary:
How each output publishes its images, by the output's name:
`reference` (the address of the file where it is, the default), `copy`
(a copy of the file beside the output) or `data-uri` (the file's
content written into the address). `copy` and `data-uri` need a way to
read image files, which the program must supply.

entries.name: graphics.convert
entries.summary:
The conversion rules of each output, by the output's name, applied
under `copy` and `data-uri` and never under `reference`. Each rule has
`from` (a format or a list of formats among `png`, `jpeg`, `gif`,
`webp`, `svg`, `pdf`), `to` (one format), `via` (the names of the
converters allowed; any converter where empty) and `options` (`dpi`,
`transparent_bg`). For each image, the first rule whose `from` lists
the image's format applies. No rule by default.

entries.name: graphics.magnification
entries.summary:
The magnification of each output, by the output's name: `raster` and
`vector`, each a number greater than zero (1 where not given), by
which every dimension of a raster or a vector image shown on that
output is multiplied, including the `width` and `height` the author
gave. An image whose type is not known uses `vector`. No
magnification by default.

entries.name: floats.types
entries.summary:
The float types, in order; no two have the same name. In settings, a
map from each type's name to its fields.

entries.name: cells.global
entries.summary:
Whether the `cells` environment is an ordinary environment of the
document, in addition to its declaration in the scoped package
`ENVIRONMENT_PACKAGE`. `false` by default.

entries.name: citations.placement
entries.summary:
Where the citation entries are shown: listed after the content, the
default, or in the citation marks in place of the numbers
(`CitationPlacement`).

entries.name: citations.mark
entries.summary:
How a citation mark shows its numbers under the listed placement, and
how the list of cited works labels its entries: `MarkForm::Bracketed`
by default. It has no effect under `CitationPlacement::InPlace`.

entries.name: citations.style
entries.summary:
The citation counter style, a counter style
(`CounterStyleDecl`): how a number is written, the delimiters, the
texts joining several numbers, whether consecutive numbers make a
range, and the words `\R` writes before a citation mark. By default
(`default_style`): arabic numbers, `[` and `]`, the compact join,
ranges on, the words `ref.~` and `refs.~`, and the variant `capital`
with the words `Ref.~` and `Refs.~`.

entries.name: citations.heading_title
entries.summary:
The title of the heading above the list of cited works, as FLM text:
`References` by default; `None` for a list with no heading above it
(`without_heading`).

entries.name: citations.heading_level
entries.summary:
The level of the heading above the list of cited works, counted from
zero like every heading level; 2 by default, the level of the heading
above a list of footnotes. The feature passes it to the heading
unchanged, and accepts every value. It has no effect on a list with no
heading.

entries.name: citations.note_separator
entries.summary:
The text written between a group's numbers and its note, as FLM text:
`; ` by default, as in `[1; Thm 4]`.

entries.name: userdefs.macros
entries.summary:
The macros: a map from a macro's name, without the backslash, to its
definition. The order written is kept.

entries.name: userdefs.environments
entries.summary:
The environments: a map from an environment's name to its definition.
The order written is kept.

entries.name: userdefs.specials
entries.summary:
The special character sequences: a map from the characters of a
sequence to its definition. The order written is kept.

entries.name: userdefs.recursion_limit
entries.summary:
The expansion depth limit: how many expansions one chain of use sites
may nest before a use site is reported with
`flm.userdefs.recursion-limit`. The default is 32
(`UserdefsConfig::recursion_limit`).

entries.name: toc.depth
entries.summary:
The deepest heading level listed: a heading is listed when its level is at
most this number. 3 by default (sections, subsections, subsubsections).

entries.name: pieces.include
entries.summary: Pieces placed although they are declared off by default.

entries.name: pieces.exclude
entries.summary: Pieces declared on by default that the render request leaves out.

entries.name: text.width
entries.summary: The line width in columns; `None` never wraps. The default is 80.

entries.name: text.tab_width
entries.summary:
The width of a tab in columns: how far a line indented by one
tab (one `\indent`
in a lines section of a quotation) is indented. The default is 4. Every
length, in any unit, is converted to columns by
`columns`.

entries.name: text.run_in_stop
entries.summary:
The stop written after the title of a run-in heading (a heading set at
the start of the paragraph it introduces), so that `\paragraph{Note} Some
content.` is printed as `Note. Some content.` The default is
`DEFAULT_RUN_IN_STOP`,
a period; the empty text writes no stop.

entries.name: text.link_addresses
entries.summary:
Whether a link to an address outside the document prints that address
after its content, between angle brackets: `\href{https://example.com}{Click
here}` prints `Click here <https://example.com>`. The default is `true`.
Off, every link prints its content alone, which keeps a text holding
many links readable. A link to a place inside the document prints its
content alone either way.

entries.name: text.link_addresses_when_shown
entries.summary:
Whether a link whose content already shows its address also prints the
address after it. A `\url` or an `\email` is such a link: its content
is derived from the address by the lowering rule that produced the
link, which sets
`LinkPayload::shows_target`.
With this option off (the default), `\url{https://example.com}` prints
`example.com`; on, it prints `example.com <https://example.com>`. It
has no effect when `link_addresses` is off.

entries.name: text.root_heading_level
entries.summary:
The heading level the text output writes as its first-level heading.
A heading's level is a number counted from zero, smaller for an outer
heading
(`HeadingPayload::level`).
A heading at this level is underlined with `=`, a heading one level
deeper with `-`, and every deeper heading is preceded by `#`
characters, one
more than its depth below this level as
`heading_depth` counts
it from 0: three for a heading two levels below. The default is
`DEFAULT_ROOT_HEADING_LEVEL`,
1, the level of a section, the same as for the HTML backend's option of
the same name
(`HtmlRenderOptions::root_heading_level`).

entries.name: latex-recomposed.unicode
entries.summary:
What is written for a non-ASCII character of document text:
`Declare`, the default, writes the character
itself as UTF-8 and declares it once in the style file;
`Replace` writes its LaTeX spelling in place
(see `escape`). Mathematics
and verbatim content are written byte for byte in either mode.

entries.name: latex-recomposed.unicode_overrides
entries.summary:
Per-character spellings that replace the spellings of the
Unicode-to-LaTeX table of `untechxt` (the table that
gives each character a LaTeX spelling and states what that spelling
needs), in either Unicode mode: for each character, the
LaTeX to write in its place, or to declare it with. Empty by default.

entries.name: latex-recomposed.drop_comments
entries.summary:
Whether the document's source comments are left out of the recomposed
LaTeX. Off by default: a comment is written with its comment prefix,
its text and the whitespace that followed it.

entries.name: latex-recomposed.skip_packages
entries.summary:
LaTeX packages that this library never requests, each given by the
name `\usepackage` takes (`amsmath`), for a user whose document class
loads them already. Empty by default.

entries.name: latex-recomposed.extra_packages
entries.summary:
LaTeX packages that the style file always requests, each a package name
with the options it is loaded with, as a `LatexPackageDef`. Empty by
default.

entries.name: latex-recomposed.extra_preamble
entries.summary:
LaTeX text written into the style file exactly as given, in three
parts (`ExtraPreamble`), all empty by default.

entries.name: latex-recomposed.bare_names
entries.summary:
The user-definition names (macro and environment names) that the
recomposed LaTeX writes exactly as the document spelled them, instead of
under the prefix that every recomposed user definition otherwise takes.
Empty by default; a name is given without a backslash, and one entry
applies to a macro and an environment of that name alike.

entries.name: latex-recomposed.robust_names
entries.summary:
The user-definition names written as **robust** LaTeX commands rather
than as the plain expandable macros that every recomposed definition
otherwise becomes. Empty by default; a name is given without a
backslash, and one entry applies to every definition of that name: a
macro, an environment, and both per-mode definitions of a name declared
once for text mode and once for mathematics mode.

entries.name: latex-recomposed.style_stem
entries.summary:
The stem of the style file's name: the style file's own name is
`<stem>.<hash>`, where the hash is computed from the file's content
(`content_hash`).
Without a naming of files by the program, the file is
`<stem>.<hash>.sty`; the program's naming of files may add to that
name, for instance a prefix from the name of the document's file
(`paper-flmrecomposed.1a2b3c4d.sty`).
The default is `DEFAULT_STYLE_STEM`, `flmrecomposed`.

entries.name: latex-recomposed.style_file
entries.summary:
When the style file is written: `WhenNeeded`,
the default, only where the document needs something in it, or
`Always`. In both cases the file is written when
`extra_packages` holds a request or any of the
three parts of `extra_preamble` is not empty,
because the author asked for something to be in it.

entries.name: latex-recomposed.heading_hook
entries.summary:
Whether a heading is written through the LaTeX hook `\flmHeading` (a
macro that the style file defines with a default and that a user may
redefine; see `preamble`).
On by default.

entries.name: latex-recomposed.label_hooks
entries.summary:
Whether labels and references are written through the LaTeX hooks
`\flmLabels`, `\flmLabelsWithDisplayText` and `\flmRef` (macros that
the style file defines with a default and that a user may redefine;
see `preamble`). On by
default.

entries.name: latex-recomposed.drop_math_labels_without_refs
entries.summary:
Whether the labels written on the lines of a display-math environment
are left out of the recomposed LaTeX **in a registry that does not hold
the references feature**. Off by default.

entries.name: latex-recomposed.resolved_proof_refs
entries.summary:
Whether a proof's **back-reference** is resolved into LaTeX hooks (on)
or written as the author wrote it over the `phfthm` package (off, the
default); the choice also decides which LaTeX package declares the
theorem-like environments. The back-reference is the title
`[*thm:x]`, which shows the statement that a proof proves, or
`[**thm:x]`, which records the relation without showing it. Off by
default.

entries.name: latex-rendered.style_stem
entries.summary:
The stem of the style file's name, `flmx` by default. The file is
named `<stem>.<hash>.sty`, `<hash>` being eight hexadecimal digits of
its content's digest, to which the program's naming of files may add a
prefix (`paper-flmx.1a2b3c4d.sty`).

entries.name: latex-rendered.run_in_stop
entries.summary:
The stop written after a run-in heading's title and a run-in
decoration's content, as the key `stop`, `.` by default; empty for
none. It is not written where the title already ends in sentence
punctuation.

entries.name: latex-rendered.skip_packages
entries.summary:
LaTeX packages this backend never requests, each given by the name
`\usepackage` takes, for a template that loads them itself. Empty by
default. A package listed here is left out of the style file's
package block, whoever requested it; listing `hyperref` leaves out
the line that loads it at the end of the preamble. The author's own
requests (`extra_packages`) are not left out.

entries.name: latex-rendered.extra_packages
entries.summary:
LaTeX packages the style file always requests, with their options,
merged after the requests the document's content causes into one
`\RequirePackage` line per package. Empty by default.

entries.name: latex-rendered.extra_preamble
entries.summary:
Three parts of LaTeX text written byte for byte into the style file:
after the engine check, after the line loading `hyperref`, and at the
end. Empty by default.

entries.name: html.title
entries.summary:
The page's title when the document states none: the words written into
`<title>` (the output region `title`) when
the render places no title piece
(`flm.meta.title`) or the title
piece holds no words. The default is `DEFAULT_TITLE`.

entries.name: html.lang
entries.summary:
The page's language as a language tag (`en`, `de-CH`), written as the
`lang` attribute of `<html>` (the output region
`lang`). `None`, the default, writes no
attribute, because a page that claims a language it is not written in is
worse for a reader using a screen reader than one that claims none.

entries.name: html.source_spans
entries.summary:
Whether the emitter writes the attribute `data-flm-source-span`, which
records where in the source a node was written, on the element it
writes for each node.

entries.name: html.run_in_stop
entries.summary:
The stop written after the title of a run-in heading, so that
`\paragraph{Note} Some content.` reads as `Note. Some content.` A
run-in heading is a heading set at the start of the paragraph it
introduces, on the paragraph's first line
(`headings`). The default is
`DEFAULT_RUN_IN_STOP`,
a period; the empty text writes none.

entries.name: html.definitions
entries.summary:
The deliveries the host gives in place of the declared content of
style and script definitions, by definition identifier
(`DefinitionOverride`). Empty by default: every definition is then
delivered as its declaration says.

entries.name: html.required_definitions
entries.summary:
The style and script definitions the host requires for the page as a
whole, by identifier, in addition to those the document's content
requires. Empty by default: a page then carries exactly what its content
needs.

entries.name: html.heading_tags
entries.summary:
The tag a block heading of each heading kind is written with, keyed by
the heading kind's name (`section`), the tag written without angle
brackets (`h2`). Empty by default. A heading kind the map does not
list is written `<h1>` to `<h6>` by its level
(`root_heading_level`).

entries.name: html.root_heading_level
entries.summary: The heading level the page writes as its first-level heading, `<h1>`.

name: argument-role
what: An argument role is a registered name for what an argument of a command holds, such as a label or a file path.

entries.name: flm.refs.target
entries.summary: The label, or several labels separated by commas, that a reference points to, each written `type:label` (`sec:intro`).

entries.name: flm.refs.defined-label
entries.summary: A label attached to a construct, written `type:label` (`sec:intro`), by which references point to the construct.

entries.name: flm.href.address
entries.summary: The address of a link: a URL, or an email address for `\email`.

entries.name: flm.defterm.defined-term
entries.summary: A term that a definition defines, by which term links point to the definition.

entries.name: flm.defterm.target
entries.summary: The term that a term link points to.

entries.name: flm.graphics.path
entries.summary: The path of an image file.

entries.name: flm.citations.key
entries.summary: Citation keys, each identifying a cited work, separated by commas.

entries.name: flm.input.path
entries.summary: A reference to another file, usually its path, whose content is read in where the command is written.
